results.label: sol-u
results.content: Main theorem. For a manifold-dependent K_0, every K at least K_0, a sequence f_n in the spectral window, a non-zero compact submanifold with smooth possibly empty boundary, and independent real X_n with a positive lower bound on E|X_n| and a finite upper bound on E|X_n|^2: (1) the expectation of the supremum of the truncated sum is equivalent to the dyadic Salem-Zygmund sum for every N with constants independent of N; (2) almost sure convergence in C^0 of the submanifold is equivalent to the Salem-Zygmund series being finite; (3) the sphere case with eigenspaces, where K is irrelevant.
results.proof_location: no proof at the statement; assembled in Sections 11-12 from Propositions 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23, with the Gaussian input from Theorems 2 and 3
results.owner_disposition: Theorem1/nonGaussianextension andProp19/22/23 use the same Gaussian criterion, original chi-radial representation, contraction/Kahane-Khintchine, elementary concavity/Jensen and Marcus-Pisier truncation. Source1636-1642 absorbs a uniformly small chi tail using its fourth moment; AppendixA gives elementary chi moments. No additional advanced core after the Gaussian criterion and declared named tools. Theorem11/Props12-14/AppendixB are the old2100 explicit covered spectral input and are not regraded.

results.label: sol
results.content: Gaussian case. Three assertions are equivalent: almost sure convergence of the Gaussian series in C^0 of the submanifold; the Salem-Zygmund condition; finiteness of the Dudley entropy integral. A sphere paragraph replaces the window by eigenspaces.

results.label: sol-q
results.content: Quantitative Gaussian version. The expectation of the supremum over the submanifold is equivalent, with a multiplicative loss depending only on the manifold, the submanifold and K, to both the Salem-Zygmund number and the entropy integral; the supremum is defined through countable subsets.

results.label: indep-met
results.content: The Pisier space is independent of the spectral parameter K, for K large, and of the Riemannian metric on the manifold.

results.label: lem-ref
results.content: Abstract metric-space entropy lemma. For a Borel probability measure with a two-sided growth bound on balls, and a pseudo-distance equivalent to Upsilon of the metric, the finiteness of the entropy integral is equivalent to the finiteness of the integral of Upsilon(t) over t sqrt(ln(1/t)). Four-step proof at 504-577: pseudo-inverse, ball-count bounds, Stieltjes integration by parts, removal of the diameter parameter.
results.owner_disposition: Completeauthorinput/partofsingleGaussiancriterion, no additionalID.

results.label: lem-quant

results.label: pro-s+
results.content: Sphere cluster pseudo-distance. For d at least 2 and theta in (0, pi/2) there is C depending only on d and theta such that, uniformly in n and in the centre, the pseudo-distance built from the eigenspace of eigenvalue -n(n+d-1) is equivalent to min(1, n delta_g) on the closed geodesic ball of radius theta. The proof at 619-658 reduces to the reproducing kernel, the addition theorem and Jacobi polynomials.
results.owner_disposition: Distinct sphere single-eigenspace/cap claim, not a literal duplicate or a direct specialization of old2100's widened spectral window. The review recommends lower-edgeH2, but the owner applies a stricter threshold after reading668-766: named Jacobi derivative/oscillatory bounds and uniform Jacobi-Bessel convergence already supply the estimates. Remaining732-765 obtains a fixed off-zero gap from the Poisson representation, unique maximum/Riemann-Lebesgue and compact uniform-convergence stability, then joins fixed scales and absorbs finitely many n by compactness. No further nonroutine asymptotic/remainder estimate is established there. Preserve the full proof as a genuine input, but do not independently countH2; this is calibration, not a correctness verdict or a duplicate claim.

results.label: jacobi
results.content: Uniform two-sided estimate for the difference of the two Jacobi polynomial values, normalised by n^(d/2-1) min(1, n^2 (1-alpha)), for alpha at least cos(2 theta). Four-step proof at 668-766: compactness gives an n-dependent bound; the mean value theorem with classical Jacobi estimates covers angles up to c1/n; Szego's uniform bound covers angles from c3/n to pi minus c3/n; Step 4 closes the gap between c1/n and c3/n by the uniform Bessel limit at the drifting scale t/n, the Poisson representation, and the strict positivity gap below the value at 0.

results.label: pseudo-dis
results.content: Manifold cluster pseudo-distance. There are K_0 and C depending only on the manifold such that for every K at least K_0, every n and every pair of points, the cluster pseudo-distance of the window is equivalent to min(1, K n delta_g), on the whole manifold and with no geometric assumption. This is the object of existing record 2100, aligned by label, printed number and the fixed spans.

results.label: minn

results.label: mino2
results.content: Scale below one wavelength. For a small beta_0, a distance below beta_0 over K n implies the cluster pseudo-distance is equivalent to K n delta_g. Six-step proof at 912-1059: convexity radius, atlas compactness, geodesic double integral with mixed derivatives, second-order comparison with the principal term, second derivative of the principal term through the Poisson representation, and the resulting quadratic bounds with K tending to infinity.

results.label: con-nec
results.content: Gaussian preliminaries. Convergence of the squared norms, L^2 convergence at a point and almost sure convergence at a point are equivalent; then the sum is a Gaussian process whose Dudley pseudo-distance is the weighted sum of the partial pseudo-distances. The proof also records the sphere kernel diagonal and the uniform bound on the sphere partial pseudo-distances.
results.owner_disposition: Completeauthorinput/partofsingleGaussiancriterion, no additionalID.

results.label: casSd
results.content: Sphere criterion. For a Gaussian process on the sphere whose covariance is a continuous function of the scalar product, three conditions are equivalent: finiteness of the integral of the square root of the covariance decrement over t sqrt(ln(1/t)); sample continuity on the sphere; and sample boundedness on one fixed geodesic arc. Proof at 1198-1251 uses the Schoenberg expansion in Jacobi polynomials, Proposition 9 on caps, Proposition 6, and in the converse direction the stationarity of the restriction to a closed geodesic together with a covering-number comparison on a sub-arc.
results.owner_disposition: Completeauthorinput/partofsingleGaussiancriterion, no additionalID.

results.label: ieii
results.content: Sphere equivalence between almost sure convergence and the Salem-Zygmund condition. Step 1 transfers a process on a curve to the geodesic arc by the Slepian comparison theorem. Step 2, the analytic core at 1301-1338, cuts the integral into dyadic blocks, splits each block into a low-frequency part and a tail, and proves that the low-frequency contribution is controlled by the tail via a two-parameter Cauchy-Schwarz argument and the bound on the maximum of two dyadic tails.
results.owner_disposition: Completeauthorinput/partofsingleGaussiancriterion, no additionalID.

results.label: ieii2
results.content: Sphere equivalence between almost sure convergence and the entropy condition. The forward direction decomposes the submanifold into finitely many pieces of diameter below pi/2 and uses subadditivity and multiplicativity of covering numbers.
results.owner_disposition: Completeauthorinput/partofsingleGaussiancriterion, no additionalID.
